ncrs.description: The  adapters of EX50066R and EX50051R (AC34040) and EX50054R (AC34041) were assembled, but the tab washers of these adapters remained open. Then, with these tab washers unlocked, the B01/B02 tests were performed on the valves of these lines, with satisfactory results.  The adapters remain on board with the tab washers unlocked and ICN requests guidance on the next steps to validate the B05 of these ACs.  NOTE: at the time of assembly, there was no B11-38 for these adapters (it was received after validation of the tests on these lines).
ncrs.currentSituation:
There was two problems to solve:
1)The issue originated from the installation of adapters EX50066R and EX50051R (AC34040) and EX50054R (AC34041) with unlocked tab washers, which did not comply with the assembly requirements defined in SEFC 33-04-21/I794E.

Although the initial B01 and B02 pressure tests were successfully completed and demonstrated no leakage, the absence of locked tab washers led to the opening of the NCR and subsequent technical reviews by ICN, NG, and ARE.

Corrective actions were later implemented:

- The tab washers were locked/bent.
B01 and B02 pressure tests were repeated, confirming leak-tightness.

- Required regression activities were performed, including B01/B02 retests and associated inspections. M05 inspections were completed.

2) We didn't apply B11-38 for the torque for the addapters EX50066R and EX50051R (AC34040) and EX50054R (AC34041). The ICN validates assembly with the quarter-turn for torque, without B11 filled, according preceding Sbr's.
ncrs.whyNotPossible:
For the problem of torque:
The latest NG decision (17 June 2026) states that the NCR can be considered conditionally closed, provided that:

1. No leakage is identified during the relevant STW activities.

2. A RIC is issued to formally confirm the absence of leakage.

3. A derogation remains active to manage watertightness requirements until completion of the affected STW scope.

4. The derogation is closed after successful validation of the RIC.

Additionally, the NCR remains linked to the progress of NCR-ICN-ESC-14-1153-2026 (replacement of EX00040).
ncrs.arguments: Final closure pending STW monitoring, RIC validation, and completion of the dependency NCR-ICN- ESC-14-1153-2026. (hydraulic motor)
ncrs.archAnswer:
EX Functional test can not be done before J06.
Hydraulic circuit of windlass to be isolated. To be mentioned into System Limitations & Temporary

instructions.

ncrs.description: The pressure reducing valve EV02105 is not maintaining its setting and is allowing pressurized air to pass through.
ncrs.currentSituation:
The valve has become defective despite having been repaired twice. It has therefore been decided that the valve must be replaced.

The valve is responsible for maintaining the 6 bar pressure required for the operation of the EV system.

To ensure system functionality, the operator manually opens the valve and monitors the system until the required pressure of 6 bar is reached.
Once the system has been pressurized under operator supervision, the valve is closed, and the system remains pressurized.
ncrs.whyNotPossible: There is currently no confirmed delivery date. No spare part available
ncrs.arguments:
Although the valve is losing its calibration, the system can be monitored during pressurization and is not continuously operated.

ICN recommends including in the temporary instructions that the system should only be used under constant supervision, with specialized personnel continuously monitoring the pressure to prevent potential damage to other components of the EV system.
The system can continue to be operated under this procedure until the new pressure-reducing valve is delivered.
ncrs.archAnswer:
Pressure reducing EV02105 not available.
Pressurization is then adjusted manually and isolated.
Pressurization of EV_BB circuit and level in EV02100 tank to be verified periodicaly. To be included in System Limitations &Temporary Instructions.

ncrs.description: BF02502 (CVT)  Non-Conformities: Test MRC-000BFM000-T011  During the execution of tests SBR- MRC-000BFM0000-T011, the following discrepancies were identified in Item 1.5.6 and Item 1.7.4  1- Failure in Diagnostic LED Indication (Fan M42) Procedure: Opening fuses F41 and F42 to verify if the red LED "Fan Defective" lights up on the PCB26 board.  Anomaly: The LED remained off. The system did not signal the failure of fan M42 as expected.  2-Undue Isolation Alarm (Backup Outlet)  Procedure: Closing circuit breakers D1 and D2 to await system stabilization. Anomaly: The converter immediately presented the "Backup outlet isolation" fault on the MMI panel, without a low insulation simulation being performed. The error occurs prematurely and unduly.  3-Operational Irregularity in Fan M41  Additional Observation: It was identified that fan M41 is operating constantly at high speed, even without the presence of active faults in the converter or thermal demand that justifies the maximum regime.
ncrs.currentSituation:
During the execution of test procedure SBR-MRC-000BFM0000-T011, non-conformities were identified affecting the monitoring and operation of the converter.

A failure in the diagnostic indication of fan M42 was observed, as the system did not activate the “Fan Defective” LED when a fault condition was simulated. Additionally, an undue “backup outlet isolation” alarm was triggered without any insulation fault simulation, indicating incorrect fault detection.

Operational anomalies were also identified in both fans:

- M41 operating continuously at high speed without demand

-M42 presenting status signal failure

Following investigation, faults were confirmed in the internal control of both fans, and replacement of M41 and M42 has been defined as required.

The previously identified insulation issue has now been resolved. Further verification will be completed after component replacement and final functional testing.
ncrs.whyNotPossible: No spare part available. FOB DATE 15/08
ncrs.arguments:
Both fans are currently operational and functioning. The identified issue is related to the lack of fault indication in the event of a fan failure, which justifies the need to replace the control board.
As a mitigating measure, a temporary instruction can be implemented, requiring periodic(daily) verification to ensure that the fans remain operational.
ncrs.archAnswer:
BF02502 (CVT) remains operrational but with anomalies under investigation.
1/ Fan M42 presenting status signal failure 2/ Undue Insulation Alarm (Backup power supply sockets)
3/ Fan M41 operating continuously at high speed without demand To be included in System Limitations & Temporary Instructions for information, and in particular for point 1/ which request a periodic (daily) verification of functionning.

ncrs.description: During test M09 (MAT211-0224) for equipment EX00040, damage occurred to the hydraulic motor flange, as shown in the attached photos.  Details of the incident:  When pressurizing the equipment as per item 6.4.1.1, the leak at inlet F prevented pressurization to the correct pressure. The team member then installed a plug at outlet F. The damage occurred when the pressure reached approximately 230 bar.
ncrs.currentSituation: The root cause has been identified as an improper test configuration that resulted in excessive pressure being applied to the motor drain circuit. The damaged hydraulic motor and potentially affected seals and fasteners must be replaced, followed by restoration and validation testing. The windlass can only be released for reinstallation onboard SBR4 after successful completion of all repairs and verification tests. If any test result is non-compliant or if operational issues remain, the equipment must be returned to Naval Group Brest for complete rework under a new NCR.
ncrs.whyNotPossible:
No spare part available.
Hydraulic motor must be replace or repaired.
ncrs.arguments:
EX00040 hydraulic motor will not be functional during the J06 period.

The piping system connected to the equipment has been properly isolated and secured, and Procedure M05 has been successfully executed.

However, to ensure the safety and integrity of the oil circuit, valves EX00175, EX00176, EX00177, EX00178, and EX00179 must remain in the closed position during undocking operations and while the vessel remains alongside the quay, until the windlass hydraulic motor has been replaced.

Although the cracked flange will not be submerged, the damaged area will be temporarily protected and sealed using tape and epoxy coating to prevent further deterioration and maintain system integrity.

Evidence of the implemented safeguards, equipment condition, and isolation measures is provided in RIC-3395, including photographs of equipment EX00040 (SBR-04).
ncrs.archAnswer:
The requirement for J06  regarding EX is compliance of the SUSP (FV1) Ok with the situation according RIC-3395
Waiver Accepted

ncrs.description: NCR opened to formalize the use of the temporary drain and the stud bolts manufactured at ICN for the maintenance of pump EM00002 (pump removed from SBR3 to be installed in SBR4).
ncrs.currentSituation: The maintenance work on pump EM00002 has been successfully executed and validated using the temporary drain and ICN-manufactured stud bolts. The equipment is operating as expected, and the implemented solution has fulfilled its intended purpose.
ncrs.whyNotPossible: The NCR remains open solely to track the receipt and installation of the definitive materials associated with NCR-MAT-006127-2025. Once the permanent components are received and installed, the temporary items will be replaced, and the NCR can be closed.
ncrs.arguments: There is currently no impact on system operation. Following execution and validation of the maintenance activities, the system remains in nominal condition and continues to perform as intended.
ncrs.archAnswer: Waiver Accepted
